scope: Source and documentation reading only; FDM; no tests, builds, simulators, browsers, hardware or credentials; no printer commands. 'Confirmed' means confirmed by reading source at the base, not observed at runtime.

findings.claim: The only executable command contract is pause: capability actions is the literal tuple ['pause'], command v2 action is the literal 'pause' with purpose 'printer-pause'. Resume, cancel, start and upload have no schema, capability or driver.

The v1 verifier authorizeCommand and PersistentReplayStore have no callers under packages, apps or scripts (tests only). It is the only place resume, cancel and emergency_stop exist as actions; project documentation describes it as a library prototype without driver or transport.
The Connector does not read the capability role field during admission; role is constrained by schema and issuer signature only. No role-per-action table exists in the Connector.

Journal rows with status outcome-unknown have null retain_until and are never deleted; cleanup covers not-sent and applied only. A claimed, write-started or outcome-unknown row makes later commands for the same assignment or printer fail as assignment-busy. No reconciliation code was found.

The driver boundary is coupled to Moonraker in three places: the local assignment schema requires moonraker_origin, the router calls openFixedMoonrakerPause directly, and the runtime accepts a single control assignment. The PauseDriver interface itself does not mention Moonraker.

Cached authority lives 30 s by default and 60 s at most, in memory only, and starts stale after restart. Only the credential-authenticated Connector inbox reaches confirm(); server_seq must strictly increase and a revocation raises the floor.

connector.authority-confirm and connector.authority-revoked frames carry no signature of their own; provenance rests on the TLS connection and credential admission. The server rereads authority every 5 s.
Verifier and dispatcher latch a wall/monotonic baseline at the first sample; skew above 1000 ms sets clockBroken and no code path resets it.

Public printer state allows idle, printing, paused, error and offline; there is no unknown or unsupported value. The Moonraker reader maps webhooks.state startup to offline. The control observation has unknown but the pause driver never emits it: states other than printing, paused and error become idle.

WebRTC peers are created with iceServers: []. The control binding rejects SDP with a typ relay candidate and requires exactly one SHA-256 DTLS fingerprint. Role proofs use separate keys and algorithms (browser ECDSA P-256, Connector Ed25519) over a domain-separated payload that includes the role.
The Connector private key is encapsulated in ConnectorIdentity; callers receive purpose-specific signing operations, not the key. Directory and files are created with modes 0o700 and 0o600.
The issuer keyring is local configuration, capped at eight entries, with an https origin; no issuer comes from the peer or the command.
The dispatcher never resends. Missing response, unconfirmed state, driver contract breach or failure to persist the result end as outcome-unknown.

The pause driver and origin validation carry no Moonraker API header, token or login; a bounded search for api_key, oneshot, authorization and access_token in packages/connector/src/moonraker and related config files returned nothing. Official Moonraker documentation states untrusted clients need a JWT or API key.
No occurrence of Anycubic, Bambu or Creality in TypeScript files under packages, apps and tests (case-insensitive).
Server issuance rereads session, membership and role, browser key, Connector enrollment, credential and assignment inside one transaction before signing a capability.

risks.risk: One outcome-unknown result blocks further pause on that printer until manual intervention in local storage; no reconciliation procedure exists in code.
The v1 schema lists resume, cancel and emergency stop, which may be mistaken for an authorized execution path; it has caller-supplied context and no transport or driver.
Roles are equivalent for every action unless a role-per-action rule is added before a second command.
The current contract cannot represent unknown or per-device unsupported; startup is reported as offline and other states as idle.
The local printer assignment only describes an http or https Moonraker origin; a different local protocol does not fit without changing the component that anchors target authorization.
Moonraker installations that require authorization are not served; there is no local store for printer credentials.
Accumulated clock skew disables pause until the process restarts. The roughly 14 h figure in project documentation was not measured here.
One control assignment per Connector: multi-printer farms have no pause path for every printer with the current composition.

hypotheses.claim: Manufacturer local protocols may not allow the single-send-on-the-same-synchronous-stack guarantee required by PauseDriver.
Manufacturer protocols may not offer strictly ordered state reads comparable to eventtime, preventing the same applied confirmation rule.
Absence of Moonraker authentication may extend to modules outside the bounded search of F14.
A compromised TLS terminator between server and Connector could forge authority-confirm; not tested.
Claimed rows left by a process crash block the assignment like outcome-unknown; indicated by the SQL, not executed.
Browser-side behaviour and the unread parts of pause-command-relay.ts match project documentation.
Connector credential renewal and revocation behave as described in docs/CONNECTOR-REVOCATION-CHECKPOINT.md; code not read.

acceptance_constraints.rule: Authority only over the browser-Connector WebRTC path: no TURN, no relay candidate, no HTTP or server command path; degraded mode is read-only.
The Connector-printer hop is separate: a local protocol is allowed there but never carries, replaces or extends browser-Connector authority.

One capability per action: start, upload, pause, resume and cancel are distinct, each with a versioned schema, its own purpose and its own signature domain prefix. No generic action, G-code or arbitrary payload.
The v1 verifier is not a production path; do not wire authorizeCommand to a driver without authenticated context, issued capability and journal equivalent to v2.
Role is decided at issuance and signed; every new action states which roles receive it and the Connector rejects a capability whose role is not allowed for the action.
Targets come only from local provisioning: no address, port, identifier or printer credential arrives by command, capability, WebRTC peer or server; targets pass a local allowlist.
Identity and capabilities are per device and firmware, never per brand; a missing feature is unsupported for that device.
Unknown is not offline: unknown, offline, stale and unsupported are distinct states; an adapter that cannot determine state publishes unknown and denies command eligibility.
Journal before effect: every command is durably claimed before any device write; journal and replay never grant authority.
At most one send, no retry: a timeout does not prove rejection; an uncertain result is outcome-unknown, visible and never resent automatically.
applied requires a later observation on the same connection and generation within the freshness bound; transport acknowledgement alone is insufficient.
Bounds preserved: capability 30 s, admission 8 s, command 5 s, fresh state 2 s, cached authority 60 s; an adapter must not widen them for a slow protocol.
Fail closed on outage: without recent server confirmation every command is refused; restart starts without authority; revocation is immediate and cannot be undone by an older confirmation.
Printer credentials never reach logs, public fixtures, diagnostics or browser DTOs; diagnostics use closed reason sets.
Bounded canonical input: every device or peer message has byte, depth and value limits and is rejected when malformed.
No command to a physical printer in automated tests; physical validation is a manual, authorized step identified by equipment and firmware.

gaps: No execution: tests, aggregate checks, simulators and hardware were not run; nothing here certifies runtime behaviour.
Partial reads: pause-command-relay.ts, pause-signalling-client.ts, pause-control-session.ts, signalling-runtime.ts and postgres-pause-authority.ts were read by excerpts and searches, not in full.
Not read: browser code under apps/farm/app, credential renewal and revocation code, camera path, telemetry queue.
CodeGraph index was not initialized in this checkout and was not created for a research-only task; bounded reads and exact searches were used, so dynamic calls may have been missed.
Local protocols of Anycubic, Bambu Lab and Creality were not studied here; no access, support or model ranking claim follows from this report.
Moonraker documentation pages show no publication date or version; the driver pins a specific Moonraker commit that was not compared with the current page.
Formatter not run: prettier is not installed in this checkout and installs were not authorized; files were formatted by hand and checked with git diff --check only.

sources.supports: Session binding, role proofs, DTLS pins, relay candidate rejection
Pause capability, policy maximums, admission proof
Local assignment, driver router, runtime composition
Methods printer.print.pause (returns ok) and printer.objects.query (eventtime, status)
Untrusted clients must use a JWT or API key
Project rules and offline authority bounds

next_steps: Decide and document the outcome-unknown reconciliation procedure before any new protocol (R1).
Propose a public state with unknown and per-device unsupported, preserving current Moonraker behaviour (R4).
Propose the smallest generalization of the local assignment: an explicit target type validated per adapter, keeping the local allowlist (R5).
Define the role-per-action table before a second command (R3).
For each candidate protocol family, answer H1 and H2 from primary documentation before designing a driver.
Mark the v1 verifier as non-production in code or remove it, as a separate task (R2).
Run the project's existing checks at the base in an authorized task and record results; this audit does not replace them.
Independent review of this report against source before using it as acceptance criteria.
